question: On a sumo tournament's last day, a 7–7 wrestler needing one more win meets an 8–6 opponent. How often does he win?
answer: About 80% of the time. Duggan and Levitt found such wrestlers won far more than their records predicted, about 49%. The eighth win secures rank and income; the opponent, already safe, has less at stake. The favour seemed to be repaid: in their next meeting, the former 7–7 wrestler won only about 40%.
move: Look for results that bend exactly where someone has most to gain.
ask: Where around me do results line up a little too neatly with who needs them?
trap: Expecting evenly matched records to produce an even contest.
reference: Mark Duggan & Steven D. Levitt, Winning Isn't Everything: Corruption in Sumo Wrestling, American Economic Review, 2002
